breaking.headline: Stock futures point to steep declines; S&P faces worst week since April 2025
breaking.fact: Nasdaq 100 futures were down 2.2% and S&P 500 futures down 1.5% ahead of Friday's open, with the Dow down 0.5%, after Thursday's 2% slide put the S&P 500 on a six-day losing streak; the indexes are on track for their worst week since April 2025, the Dow down 6.2% for the week. The 10-year yield eased to 4.98%, WTI slipped to $82.30 a barrel, gold fell to a 14-month low near $3,575 an ounce and bitcoin traded near $61,400.

breaking.headline: Asian equities tumble as AI selloff deepens; Nikkei falls 4.5%
breaking.fact: Japan's Nikkei 225 tumbled 4.54% and South Korea's Kospi fell 4.74% on Friday as the AI selloff spread across Asia, with MSCI's Asia Pacific index down for a seventh straight session; Japan's core consumer prices rose 2.2% in October, reinforcing expectations of another Bank of Japan rate hike.

breaking.headline: California subpoenas Nvidia over chips, China and investor disclosure
breaking.fact: California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia on Thursday, asking whether its advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether it misled investors, tied to reports about former CEO Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy. The release states no finding and names no statute or deadline; Nvidia had published no response by early Friday. House committees have Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter set for transcribed interviews on Dec. 1 and 2.

weekInBrief.headline: Intuit to sell Mailchimp for $3.68 billion, a third of what it paid
weekInBrief.body: Intuit said it will sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion — roughly a third of the $12 billion it paid for the marketing platform in 2021. Intuit shares fell nearly 10% on the news even though its quarterly results beat expectations on the top and bottom lines.

weekInBrief.headline: Walmart raises outlook as third-quarter revenue climbs 5.2% to $188.8 billion
weekInBrief.body: Walmart reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $188.8 billion, up 5.2% from a year earlier, and raised its full-year outlook, with net sales now expected to grow 4.9% to 5.2%. Operating income rose 16.0% to $7.77 billion, but diluted earnings per share fell 19.5% to $0.62 as a $2.4 billion swing from investment gains to losses outweighed the operating gain; U.S. eCommerce grew 23%.

weekInBrief.headline: Jobless claims edge up to 203,000; Labor Department finalizes contractor rule
weekInBrief.body: Initial jobless claims rose 1,000 to 203,000 in the week ended Nov. 14, still 8.6% below a year earlier, while the number of people staying on benefits rose 70,000 to 1,763,000. The Labor Department also finalized a rule returning independent-contractor classification to a test substantially similar to its 2021 version, taking effect 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

weekInBrief.headline: Senate passes measure to speed up energy projects, lower consumer costs
weekInBrief.body: The Senate passed a bipartisan measure designed to streamline federal permitting for energy projects and lower consumer costs. The effort split Democrats over environmental concerns, and backers say faster permitting should bring energy projects online sooner.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: A cargo of Iranian crude moved ship-to-ship in the Persian Gulf this week — the first such movement since the U.S. reinstated its blockade of Iranian ports in mid-July. The U.S.-sanctioned Suezmax Olym transferred about 200,000 barrels to the medium-range tanker Hao Fan on Tuesday just south of Iran's Kharg Island terminal, with both vessels' transponders off, according to United Against Nuclear Iran and tracker Kpler, with TankerTrackers.com reporting the same transfer. The U.S. military warned Wednesday, in JMIC Advisory 017-26, that any vessel receiving Iranian cargo at sea is now a blockade evader subject to being stopped, boarded or seized. Iranian media affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards floated sending a convoy of tankers loaded with crude to China in defiance of the blockade. On oil, a small amount of Iranian crude is moving again — about 200,000 barrels changed hands ship-to-ship on Tuesday, the first such movement since July — but it has not left the Gulf as an export, while about 8.3 million barrels a day of oil and products, effectively all non-Iranian with Iranian exports near a standstill, kept flowing through the strait in the week to November 11, about 48% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: Starship Flight 17 hardware rolls to Massey's for cryo testing
space.body: SpaceX is already preparing its next Starship flights: Ship 44 and Booster 24 — the vehicles for Flight 17 — rolled to the Massey's test site at Starbase, Texas, for cryogenic proof testing on Thursday, less than a week after Flight 15's historic orbital catch of the upper stage. Ship 43 and Booster 23, the Flight 16 pair, did their cryo tests last month, and Flight 16 could launch as soon as next month, possibly from Starbase, with Flight 17 then taking the first Starship launch from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39A. SpaceX has released no mission design or date for either flight. Musk said the recovered Ship 42 will go on public display rather than fly again.

space.headline: SpaceX disputes Starship debris claims on Mexican beaches
space.body: SpaceX has rejected claims that debris from the failed Starship booster on Nov. 13 polluted beaches on Mexico's northern Gulf coast, saying its partners found very little material and the origin of what was collected is unclear. The environmental group Conibio Global has counted more than 1,500 pieces, and Mexico's federal environmental prosecutor, Profepa, has inspected the sites, is collecting fragments of the booster's lining and is demanding SpaceX take responsibility.

space.headline: 'Game changer' blood test for CTE may be coming
space.body: Traces of a brain protein in blood could soon lead to a test that diagnoses chronic traumatic encephalopathy — the degenerative brain disease best known for affecting football players — during a person's lifetime. In two studies published in JAMA, blood tests for the protein eMTBR-tau spotted later-stage CTE in former players, 18 of 21 of whom were confirmed to have the disease after death. The test is not yet FDA-approved, and the researchers stress it is still in the discovery phase with a small sample.

space.headline: Adaptive AI agent plans and runs lab experiments on its own
space.body: Researchers at University College London, HKUST (Guangzhou) and partner institutions have built an embodied science agent that autonomously plans and conducts experiments, pairing a digital agent that learns from past results with a robotic agent that controls lab instruments. In a wastewater-treatment test it picked conditions from more than 200 million combinations and, over 15 rounds, cut residual dye by 98.5%, a step toward self-driving laboratories. The work is posted on arXiv.

apod.title: V-G-R
apod.credit: Apostolos Kyriazis — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, November 20, 2026
apod.explanation: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory read V-G-R — the call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft, now in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometres away. Travelling at the speed of light, the message would take one day to reach humanity's most distant spacecraft; Voyager 1 was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977.
